summary: All 32 unit tests pass cleanly (0.002s). Every one of the 9 original requirements is satisfied by the backend implementation: account creation, deposit/withdraw, buy/sell with quantity, portfolio valuation, P&L, holdings reporting, transaction listing, and all three guardrails (negative-balance withdrawal, unaffordable purchase, overselling). The Gradio frontend imports and validates without error. Two minor advisory findings (a design-doc vs implementation discrepancy in P&L formula, and an untested helper method) do not affect correctness or block the build.

findings.summary: get_profit_loss() formula differs from the design document specification
findings.detail: The design doc (§1.4) specifies P&L = portfolio_value − total_deposits. The implementation computes P&L = portfolio_value − (total_deposits − total_withdrawals), i.e. net invested capital. The implementation is arguably more financially correct, but the discrepancy is never caught because no test exercises P&L after a withdrawal. Either update the design doc to match the code, or align the code to the design doc and add a withdrawal‑aware P&L test.

The Account class exposes get_total_withdrawals() and get_profit_loss() relies on it internally, but no unit test directly verifies that get_total_withdrawals() returns the correct sum after one or more withdrawals. This could mask a regression in the withdrawal‑summation logic. Add a dedicated test (e.g. deposit 100, withdraw 30, withdraw 20, assert total withdrawals == 50).

findings.summary: get_profit_loss docstring mentions 'genuine profit/loss' which is slightly inconsistent with the original requirement wording
findings.detail: The docstring says 'genuine profit/loss' while requirement 4 says 'profit or loss from the initial deposit'. This is cosmetic and does not affect behaviour. Consider aligning the docstring phrasing for clarity.
